instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Rows where value is above the average
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value > (SELECT AVG(value) FROM positions);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Row with the highest value
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value = (SELECT MAX(value) FROM positions);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Row with the lowest value
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value = (SELECT MIN(value) FROM positions);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Rows where id is in a subquery from positions
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE id IN (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM positions);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Rows where id is not in the set of values 1 and 2
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE id NOT IN (1, 2);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Use EXISTS to find rows where a id appears more than once
output: SELECT * FROM positions t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM positions t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id GROUP BY t2.id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Subquery in SELECT returning count per id
output: SELECT t.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM positions t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id) AS cnt FROM positions t;

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Rows where value > the maximum of account plus 100 in subquery
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value > ((SELECT MAX(value) FROM positions) + 100);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Second highest value using subquery
output: SELECT MAX(value) FROM positions WHERE value < (SELECT MAX(value) FROM positions);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Correlated subquery: rows whose value is above the avg of their id
output: SELECT * FROM positions t WHERE value > (SELECT AVG(value) FROM positions t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Columns where value is greater than average in their group
output: SELECT * FROM positions t WHERE value >= (SELECT AVG(value) FROM positions t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Derived table returning count per id
output: SELECT sub.id, sub.cnt FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM positions GROUP BY id) sub WHERE sub.cnt > 2;

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Subquery filtering rows with ANY operator
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value = ANY (SELECT value FROM positions WHERE value < 50);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Subquery filtering rows with ALL operator
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value > ALL (SELECT AVG(value) FROM positions);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Scalar subquery for a single value
output: SELECT (SELECT AVG(value) FROM positions) AS avg_val;

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Rows matching set from a subquery using IN
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM positions GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Largest value strictly less than the global maximum
output: SELECT value FROM positions ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Nested subquery: top values per group based on derived ranking
output: SELECT t.* FROM positions t WHERE t.value = (SELECT MAX(value) FROM positions t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Rows where account not present in a sub table
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE account NOT IN (SELECT account FROM positions WHERE value > 90);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Subquery used to compare against the overall total
output: SELECT id, SUM(value) AS part FROM positions GROUP BY id HAVING SUM(value) > (SELECT AVG(value) FROM positions);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Use a subquery to compute rolling reference count
output: SELECT t.id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM positions t2 WHERE t2.id <= t.id) AS running FROM positions t;

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
EXISTS correlated check to its own table values
output: SELECT * FROM positions t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM positions t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id AND t2.value > t.value);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Subquery comparing to the minimum plus a constant
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value > (SELECT MIN(value) FROM positions) + 10;

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Subquery returning rows for a top slice group
output: SELECT * FROM positions WHERE value IN (SELECT value FROM positions ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 5);

instruction:
Schema: positions(id, account, value)
Subquery joining a derived aggregate
output: SELECT t.* FROM positions t JOIN (SELECT id, MAX(value) mx FROM positions GROUP BY id) a ON a.id = t.id AND a.mx = t.value;
